newsitem.title: CANADA: Pools say lack of rival bid for bodes well.
newsitem.headline: Pools say lack of rival bid for bodes well.

text.p: The absence of a rival bid to buy United Grain Growers Ltd showed a C$172 million hostile takeover offer by Alberta Wheat Pool and Manitoba Pool Elevators is good value, AWP's chief financial officer said.

"They (UGG) are unable to show where the value lies, nor can they identify a Canadian or foreign buyer willing to pay more than C$13.75 (a share). That tells us C$13.75 is a good value," AWP Chief Financial Officer Geoff Southwood said.
UGG said Thursday its directors formally rejected the bid announced by AWP and MPE Feb 20 when the Pools acquired 14.98 percent of UGG and unveiled a lock-up deal to buy 6.4 percent more.

A Manitoba court will decide next Tuesday and Wednesday whether the lock-up deal triggered UGG's poison pill which comes into effect when any one shareholder acquires more than 15 percent of UGG shares.
UGG stock closed Thursday at C$14 on the Toronto Stock Exchange with 21,706 shares changing hands.
Southwood said that until the offer by AWP and MPE, UGG shares on the TSE were trading in the C$10 range. The 52 week low is C$6.625 and high is C$14.50.
"The synergies obtained by integrating UGG will create a strong, Canadian, farmer-owned business," he said.
"That's why we offered $13.75, a 34 percent premium on UGG's trading range before the offer," Southwood added.
The Pools said their bid was to stave off a UGG takeover by U.S. firms. Rumors in the past year have had ConAgra Inc or Archer Daniels Midland buying up UGG.
"We have not been approached by foreign entities," UGG President Ted Allen said Thursday. Asked whether domestic firms approached UGG, he said: "Not in any substantive way."
Other Canadian grain industry observers said the Pools' bid was to prevent further incursions into their provinces by rival cooperative Saskatchewan Wheat Pool.
There are recent rumours an off-shore multinational food processor may counter the Pools' offer, grain sources said.
